description: The first line of the year

participation.context: Ruled the leaf, headed it, and wrote the first line from memory.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: the first line of the year

story.body: You opened the year's book at a fresh leaf, headed it 1594, and set down the one line about the Queen. The rest of the leaf was still empty.

relations.note: the first line of the year

title: Headed the leaf and wrote one line

relations.note: the desk, and he is not in the picture

story.body: The picture holds the open book, the one line, the writing things, and the frost. You are not in it.

relations.note: the desk, and he is not in the picture

title: Left the desk with one line on the leaf

participation.context: Wrote the rest of the leaf, and the line after the pan.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: the winter marks and the private line

story.body: You wrote the two nights, the coffer's sum, and the three marks. When the pan dropped below, you added the private line and stopped.

relations.note: the winter marks and the private line

title: Filled the leaf under the first line

story.body: You wrote Twins' day by Candlemas and rent by Lady Day. You added nothing else on those leaves.

title: Marked Candlemas as the twins' day and Lady Day as rent

participation.context: Paid both sums, named the twenty pounds as not yet had, and went up.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Named the sixpence and the threepence, took them, and sent him back to the leaf.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Apologised for the pan and offered the ink.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

relations.note: her lodger, at the foot of her stair
relations.quote: There is the sixpence, and the threepence with it.
The horn is full. Leave it.

story.body: You met Mistress Ansell and Alse at the foot of the stair. The pan was chipped. You paid sixpence for the week's firing and washing and threepence for the noon board, and you went back up.

relations.note: her lodger, at the foot of her stair
relations.quote: There is the sixpence, and the threepence with it.
The horn is full. Leave it.

title: Paid the sixpence and the threepence at the stair
